changes.after: Enrolled HB1601 would require a locality, before approval of specified zoning applications for a new high energy use facility, to require the applicant to assess its sound profile on residential units and schools within 500 feet of the property boundary, to the extent practicable and within the statutory timeline. A facility qualifies when the applicant reasonably anticipates at application that it will require 100 MW or more of retail utility power. The locality may require specified resource assessments on the site or immediately contiguous land, and must require qualified utility substation and transmission information. The existing-approval expansion or modification exception states that the expansion 'does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more'; its numeric boundary is unresolved. Existing local zoning authority is preserved. The enrolled print has blank chapter and approval fields; later post-veto proceedings remain unverified.

changes.before: Would prevent utility costs substantially related to serving data center customers of 100 MW or more from being recovered from non-data-center customers unless rates substantially recover those costs from data centers. changes.after: Introduced HB503 would bar inclusion in SCC-approved rates or charges under § 56-585.1 or § 56-585.8 of Phase I or Phase II utility costs, including increased fuel, generation and transmission costs, that are substantially related to electric service to data center customers and would not have been incurred but for their demand, unless the rates or charges are designed to recover, or substantially recover, those costs solely from data center customers. For this provision, a data center customer is a data center under § 58.1-3506(A)(43) with peak demand of 100 MW or greater.
